questions.q: What is the best framing for Power BI governance, according to this lesson?
options: Guardrails that keep self-service BI safe at scale, not a committee that blocks authors
A set of restrictions that only IT can configure, with no role for report authors
A feature exclusive to Power BI Premium capacities
A one-time setup task performed once and never revisited
questions.explain: Governance is framed as the rules and controls that let self-service BI stay safe and trustworthy as it scales — guardrails, not gatekeeping.

questions.q: Which of the four governance pillars covered in this course does 'workspaces and domains' belong to?
options: Security
Trust and lifecycle
Administration
Structure
questions.explain: Structure covers where content lives and who owns it — workspaces and domains are the core structural units.

questions.q: Where do nearly all tenant-wide Power BI governance controls live?
options: Only in Power BI Desktop, never in the service
The admin experience, reachable from the Settings gear in the Power BI service
Inside each individual report's file properties
The Microsoft Purview compliance portal exclusively
questions.explain: The admin experience (Settings gear) is the home base for tenant settings, domains, capacities, and monitoring — the lever behind most governance controls.

questions.q: What does a Power BI domain do?
options: Replaces the need for workspace roles entirely
Groups related workspaces for structure, ownership, and discoverability
Defines row-level security filters for a workspace
Encrypts data at rest inside a semantic model
questions.explain: A domain is a logical grouping of workspaces — once assigned, items in those workspaces inherit the domain attribute for filtering and discovery.

questions.q: Why is governance described as a 'distributed responsibility' in this lesson?
options: Because governance only applies to Premium capacity workspaces
Because Microsoft handles all governance automatically with no user input
Because only the tenant admin has any governance responsibility
Tenant admins, domain/workspace admins, and individual authors each own a slice of it
questions.explain: No single role owns all of governance — tenant admins set org-wide settings, domain/workspace admins manage their own scope, and every author applies RLS, labels, and sharing decisions on their own content.
